September 2, 2026

US strikes Iran again as Tehran hits American bases across the region

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

The United States carried out significant new strikes on Iran, in what was described as the largest exchange since July, with Iran targeting American bases across the Middle East in response. Iranian officials said a US strike hit a wedding in an Iranian province, killing at least five people and injuring dozens, including children. Trump posted that he is not seeking to force Iran to the bargaining table, said the US has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran's economy is collapsing, and asked when the Iranian people would rise up and fight.

Russia said to be helping Iran build supersonic missiles to target US warships

tags: war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

According to Financial Times reporting, Russia is secretly providing Iran with advanced intelligence and technical support to build supersonic cruise missiles capable of targeting American warships in the Middle East. The transfer is described as one of the most significant known movements of military technology from Moscow to Tehran. The report runs counter to Trump's public statements about his relationship with Vladimir Putin.

Defense Secretary Hegseth faces impeachment calls as Army leadership churns

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Multiple members of Congress, including Sarah McBride and Robert Garcia, said over the past 24 hours that they would support impeaching and removing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. CNN reporting indicates his focus on culture war issues is impeding the Army's progress, and he has pushed out generals who disagree with him. Army officials have resigned amid the turmoil at the Pentagon.

ICE launches AI doxing-mitigation program with ZeroFox amid whistleblower concerns

tags: surveillance, immigration
sources: @oafnation_actual

An internal agency-wide memo describes a new ICE "Doxing Mitigation Initiative" using AI cybersecurity firm ZeroFox to scan social media and the dark web for information that could identify ICE agents and officers. ICE entered into a roughly $14.6 million contract with ZeroFox last month, funded through ICE Intelligence. Insiders and experts said the technology could be used to identify whistleblowers and non-loyalists inside the agency; ZeroFox previously drew criticism for its use during the 2015 Baltimore protests and after January 6.

USPS whistleblower accuses administration of violating court order over election systems

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

A USPS official alleged that the Trump administration violated a court order and rapidly developed a system that could produce catastrophic results in the midterm elections. Separately, Tarrant County in Texas voted to cut 92 polling sites ahead of the midterms. Voter rolls are also reported to be undergoing purges in Texas.

Patagonia and tribal groups sue Trump over Bears Ears reduction

tags: legal, environment
sources: @carolinegleich

Patagonia joined A'Nuche, a nonprofit led by members of the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe, and the Conservation Lands Foundation in a federal lawsuit in Washington challenging the shrinking of Bears Ears National Monument. A July proclamation cut Bears Ears by more than 1.2 million acres, or 91 percent, and reduced Grand Staircase-Escalante by nearly 1.7 million acres. The suit argues the Antiquities Act permits a president to create monuments but not to shrink them; at least nine mining claims have already been staked on removed land.

Forest Service moves to repeal Roadless Rule covering 44 million acres

tags: environment, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

The Forest Service is moving to repeal the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule, which bars most new road construction, road reconstruction and timber harvesting across roughly 44 million acres of national forest. Repeal would not automatically open the land to logging but would remove a national safeguard and shift decisions to individual forest plans. The proposal is in a public comment period, during which the agency must respond to comments on the record.

Nepal flood recovery funding arrives as loans, not grants

tags: climate, economy
sources: @carolinegleich

A glacier collapse in the Himalaya on August 26 sent water, ice and rock down river valleys, leaving nearly 1,000 dead and about 4,200 missing, with roads, bridges and villages destroyed. The United States first announced $500,000 and later activated $3.6 million in humanitarian aid, including food support for up to 10,000 households. The World Bank has indicated up to about $164 million could be mobilized, but as loans, prompting calls for grants, debt relief and loss-and-damage finance instead.

Supreme Court to decide whether Second Amendment protects AR-15 ownership

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Supreme Court will take up a case on whether the Second Amendment protects ownership of AR-15 rifles. Gun owners have asked the court to extend constitutional protection to the weapons.

Brian Mast under consideration for Secretary of the Army

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual, @ericmoutsos

Department of War officials indicated that Congressman Brian Mast, an IDF veteran who previously wore an IDF uniform in the halls of Congress, is under consideration to replace Dan Driscoll as Secretary of the Army. Sean Parnell and Derrick Anderson are also said to be under consideration. Mast has previously made statements calling for killing terrorists and their supporters and saying more infrastructure in Gaza needs to be destroyed.

82nd Airborne deployments extended to a full year in the Middle East

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Some 82nd Airborne troops could spend up to a full year deployed in the Middle East under extended deployment orders. The extension comes amid the escalating US-Iran conflict.

USS Abraham Lincoln arrives in Thailand showing heavy wear after nine months at sea

tags: defence
sources: @aaronparnas

The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln arrived in Thailand after nine months at sea with visible rust and hull deterioration from prolonged saltwater exposure. Sailors aboard the ship reportedly faced food rationing during the extended deployment, with some service members seeking to leave. The crew will have a five-day rest period before returning to the United States.

Trump renames Lake Ontario and floats renaming the Strait of Hormuz

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Apple Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for US users following a personal call from Trump, matching a prior change by Google Maps; MapQuest has not made the change and is currently the top app in the US App Store. Trump has since suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz the "Strait of Trump" and has floated renaming the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, though no order has been signed. Previous renamings include the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America and the Department of Defense to the Department of War.

Emergency responders diverted from national parks before deadly Grand Canyon floods

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration diverted 300 specialized emergency first responders from national parks to work on a project in Washington, D.C. Days later, flash floods in the Grand Canyon killed at least two people. The CDC also scrubbed two measles deaths from its national database.

Judge rules Tyler Robinson can go to trial in Charlie Kirk killing

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A judge ruled that Tyler Robinson can proceed to trial in the killing of Charlie Kirk, where he faces the death penalty. Separately, the jury in the Lindsay Clancy case remains deadlocked and went home early.

Ed Markey wins Massachusetts Senate primary

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Senator Ed Markey won his primary in Massachusetts for Senate.

Fox News segment frames falling teen birth rate as a fertility problem

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A Fox News segment argued that declining fertility among 15-to-19-year-olds is a problem, noting the rate is down 7 percent recently and 70 percent over two decades against 3.6 million annual births. The segment attributed the decline to messaging that young people should wait until they are financially secure and in stable life situations before having children.

Republican Jewish Coalition head describes campaigns against Massie and Carlson

tags: politics, media
sources: @ericmoutsos

Leaked remarks attributed to a former US senator leading the Republican Jewish Coalition described the group's role in defeating Congressman Thomas Massie in his Kentucky primary and in publicly confronting Tucker Carlson by name. The speaker said a majority of Gen Z holds an unfavorable impression of Israel and attributed this to losing the digital information war, listing technology executives as central figures. Separately, leaked audio was said to show Vice President JD Vance pledging support to a group and speaking about doing God's work even if it leads to the end times.
